messages:
maria: saw a canary alert from eu1 this morning — p99 latency on L4 nodes doubled after the small-batch-adaptive rollout :eyes:
aj: ugh, I saw the same in dashboards. looks correlated with commit 3f2a1b4 (adaptive small-batch heuristic)
leo: thanks for flagging. is the spike only on L4/A10 or also H100?
maria: only L4 clusters in eu1 and a single dedicated A10 cluster. H100 canaries are fine.
aj: quick summary from traces: backlog builds up on egress NIC queue, packets cluster around 5-7ms gaps -> sustained small bursts. suspect microbatch churn + kernel selector flip.
maria: CI microbench showed 8% extra syscalls in matrix for small sequences after the heuristic change. snippet from the perf trace:
```
# perf top (canary-eu1-l4)
  samples  pcnt  symbol
   3123   21.4  nvme_submit
   2410   16.5  runtime::kv_cache::evict_path
   1109    7.6  scheduler::select_kernel_adaptive
```
aj: interesting that nvme shows up — might be noisy neighbor IO amplification from increased tiny writes (checkpointing kv cache). leo can you pull a flamegraph from the canary host?
leo: starting a quick flame, giving link: https://perf.internal/redwood/flames/2150123456-eu1-smallbatch (approx)
ops-bot: alert muted for 10m in #pager on request of @maria :white_check_mark:
ci-bot: note: microbench regression detected on ci/build/bench-small-seq — build 4.12.3 -> 4.13.0 (failed p99 threshold)
maria: can we bisect quickly? if it's 3f2a1b4 we should revert or flip a flag.
aj: ran git bisect locally, commit 3f2a1b4 is the first bad. suggested immediate mitigation: force legacy batch window on eu1 L4 via rollout rule.
leo: patch to toggle flag created: `revert-smallbatch-heuristic-eu1` (PR 5279). also added a temporary scheduler knob: `legacy_small_batch=true`
maria: rolling the rule to eu1-l4 canaries now, will confirm p99.
(maria later): canary rollback applied to eu1-l4, initial 10% -> 0% over 2 minutes. p99 back to baseline within 4 minutes :tada:
aj: leaving the bisect notes: root cause = adaptive heuristic reduced min_batch threshold, increasing number of microbatches for short sequences causing higher kernel-selector churn and more frequent KV checkpoint writes -> egress packetization + NIC queuing on L4 band.
leo: follow-ups: 1) add a kernel-selector debounce to avoid flip-flopping on short bursts, 2) change kv checkpoint coalescing for small evictions, 3) add egress queueing metric to canary dashboards.
maria: opened issues: https://issues.redwood/repro/ISS-8812 (debounce), ISS-8813 (kv coalesce), ISS-8814 (dashboard)
aj: we'll keep rollback PR open until PR 5279 lands and we validate across eu1/euw2.
maria: thanks all — ping me if you see further regressions. :thumbsup:
